small_guidance:
- Add larger GEMM tile configs to the autotune sweep (e.g. BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8 num_stages=3, and BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64) since M=N=K=8192 favors bigger tiles; also try num_stages=4 for K=8192 to better overlap K-loop loads.
- Transpose weight to (K, N) row-major once in `__init__` so the inner B load is contiguous along N (stride_bk = N, stride_bn = 1) instead of the current strided pattern, which should boost tl.dot throughput substantially.
- For the softmax kernel with N=8192 (BLOCK_N=8192), try num_warps=8 (instead of 16) and num_stages=2; 16 warps over a single row often underutilizes — and consider a 2-pass online softmax tiled over N to avoid allocating a huge BLOCK_N register tile.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the softmax directly into the GEMM epilogue using a persistent / split-K-free kernel that emits an entire output row per program group: pick BLOCK_N >= N (8192) so each program tile spans the full row, compute GELU on the accumulator, then do row-max and row-sum reductions across the BLOCK_N dimension before storing normalized values. This removes the full write+read of the 1024×8192 intermediate.
- Alternatively, store GELU output plus per-row (max, sum) statistics from the GEMM (one reduction across N tiles using atomics or a two-stage launch), then a lightweight second kernel only normalizes — avoiding redundant recomputation of GELU.
- Pre-transpose the Linear weight to (K, N) contiguous in `__init__` so the GEMM's B operand is laid out for coalesced inner-dim loads; this is a one-time cost that benefits every forward.
